name: French Polynesia
summary_text: French Polynesia: full French law applies; historically tolerant Ma'ohi culture (mahuu third-gender presence); tourism economy. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: France (0.67) plus a local delta of +0.00. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: The Plight Of Trans Women In Prison
sources.claim_summary: BuzzFeed News feature (Jan 2018, French context): trans women in France incarcerated on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area - relevant to French Polynesia as a French overseas collectivity applying French law.

CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (French context, applicable in French Polynesia): serious violations persist across places of detention.

sources.title: Transgender rights in Tahiti — Grokipedia
sources.claim_summary: Grokipedia page on transgender rights in Tahiti: French anti-discrimination law applies (gender-identity protections since 2012, hate crimes since 2017, conversion-therapy ban since 2022); legal gender recognition without restrictions; culturally, the māhū third-gender role predates colonisation, while modern rae-rae identities face varying stigma; transphobic violence and employment discrimination pushing some rae-rae into sex work persist.

sources.title: French Polynesia LGBTQ+ inclusivity: No need for Pride flags
sources.claim_summary: OutTraveler (April 2025): 'French Polynesia doesn't need Pride flags to earn its place on every LGBTQ+ bucket list' - openness is 'ingrained in the culture'; the māhū (traditional third gender) and rae-rae are visible in daily life; 118 islands with direct flights from major cities.

sources.title: French Polynesia reflects on LGBTQIA+ rights, place in society | RNZ
sources.claim_summary: RNZ Pacific (Dec 2023): French Polynesia held its first international colloquium on LGBTQIA+ rights ('Our voices, our rights, our Pacific Way') at the University of French Polynesia - with government, church and regional participants; recalled that the third gender (Rae-rae in French Polynesia, Faʻafafine in Samoa) is a well-entrenched, accepted part of Polynesian society.
Out Adventures gay travel guide for French Polynesia: 'a relaxed, gay-welcoming South Pacific culture' across Tahiti and Bora Bora's 118 islands - travel-oriented assessment of the destination.
